books.authorNote: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley (1797–1851) was the daughter of the philosopher William Godwin and the writer Mary Wollstonecraft. She began Frankenstein in the summer of 1816 near Geneva, during a ghost-story challenge with Lord Byron and Percy Shelley, and it was published anonymously in 1818, when she was twenty. She revised it for an 1831 edition; this is the original 1818 text. Her other novels include The Last Man (1826).

books.authorNote: Hermann Hesse (1877–1962) was a German-born novelist and poet who became a Swiss citizen. His mother was born in India and his grandfather was a missionary scholar there, and he travelled to South and Southeast Asia in 1911. Siddhartha was published in 1922. His other novels include Demian (1919), Steppenwolf (1927), and The Glass Bead Game (1943). He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1946.
